gemini.rationale: The slice documents that both companies' met- and thermal-coal products (T4), mining/processing/blending operations (T5), and workforces (T6) were brought together into a single Contura-parent vehicle at closing. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch where products transferred without their underlying processes, or processes transferred without their operating personnel.

grok.rationale: At closing the slice states both parties’ met- and thermal-coal products and their mining, processing and coal-blending operations combine into one operating footprint with ‘improved metallurgical coal blending capabilities,’ so T4 and T5 crossed together with no product-vs-process mismatch (gap_45=0). The same closing structure brings both workforces (Contura ~1,750; Alpha ~2,700) and a shared 5/4 board into the Contura-parent vehicle, so T5 and T6 likewise align with no process-vs-organization gap (gap_56=0); the pre-existing 2016 TSA is described only as an already-shared back-office bridge, not as mitigation of a closing transfer gap.

openai.rationale: The customer-facing met- and thermal-coal products of both parties crossed the boundary together with both companies’ mining, processing, and coal-blending operations, which were combined into one operating footprint; therefore no product-process structural gap is documented at closing. The slice also states that both workforces were brought into the single Contura-parent structure and that the nine-member board included five Contura directors and four Alpha designees, so no process-organization structural gap is documented.
